elements.evidence: "sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term" is deleted; replaced with "Customer may obtain hosted analytics services ... from any third party at any time."

elements.element: Any exclusivity confined to a defined product category (fallback)
elements.evidence: No exclusivity survives ('Vendor's appointment is non-exclusive'), so the limitation condition is absent.

offending_extra_words: or any other products or services
reasons: Preferred level is fully achieved: the sole-and-exclusive appointment in 2.2 is converted to non-exclusive, leaving no exclusivity or sole-supplier duty on Customer, and 12.3 is untouched.

Minimality fails: the edit rewrites the whole of 2.2 and adds an affirmative purchasing freedom broader than the rule requires ('or any other products or services', 'at any time'), duplicating protection already granted by 12.3's untouched 'Nothing restricts Customer from ... engaging any supplier'. The official minimality gate also flagged a 0.741 changed-character ratio.
A tighter edit — e.g. replacing 'sole and exclusive' with 'non-exclusive' in the original sentence — would complete the preferred level with far fewer changed characters.
Intent is preserved: no undefined terms, no dangling mechanics, and the change removes the prior contradiction between 2.2 and 12.3.
